code_findings.title: GREEN/ship-smoke timeout failures hide the timeout cause — stderr is dropped
code_findings.evidence: scripts/verify_checkpoint.py:776-778 (also :770-772, :800-802, :955-958, :1593-1596): on exit 124, _run sets stdout="" and puts 'timed out after Ns' in stderr, but these failure paths print only 'FAIL: pytest failed (exit 124)' plus stdout[-500:], which is empty on timeout
code_findings.fix: In the generic non-zero failure paths, also echo a tail of result.stderr, or special-case exit 124 with a one-line hint: '(exit 124 = timed out after {timeout}s; raise KIT_CHECKPOINT_TEST_TIMEOUT)'. In-scope-adjacent but non-blocking given the 600s default makes GREEN timeouts rare

code_findings.title: KIT_CHECKPOINT_TEST_TIMEOUT is undocumented outside the helper docstring

security_findings.title: No upper bound on KIT_CHECKPOINT_TEST_TIMEOUT: values >= ~1e9 crash the verifier with unhandled OverflowError; large-but-valid values silently remove the hang bound
security_findings.evidence: scripts/verify_checkpoint.py:70 `return value if value > 0 else _DEFAULT_TEST_TIMEOUT` — no upper clamp. Verified: KIT_CHECKPOINT_TEST_TIMEOUT=10**9 -> `OverflowError: timeout is too large` inside subprocess.run (uncaught by _run, which only handles TimeoutExpired/FileNotFoundError at scripts/verify_checkpoint.py:40-52); 10**6 works but effectively disables the timeout. Requires local env control, fails closed (crash = checkpoint failure), no gate bypass — hence Low, not Medium.
security_findings.fix: Clamp in _test_timeout(), e.g. `return min(value, 86400) if value > 0 else _DEFAULT_TEST_TIMEOUT` (optionally print a WARN when clamping). Alternatively catch OverflowError alongside TimeoutExpired in _run, but the clamp is simpler and also restores a meaningful hang bound.
